newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa firm buys Sterling Clothing.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa firm buys Sterling Clothing.

text.p: South Africa's Bengoshi Investments Ltd said on Wednesday it had bought a 53.47 percent controlling stake in embattled clothing firm Sterling Clothing Ltd at 25 cents a share from the Berman and Barbieri families.
Bengoshi, which will extend a similar offer to Sterling's minority shareholders, will be injecting capital into the firm to cut its 12 million rand debt bill.

The announcement follows a cautionary notice on Tuesday in which Sterling said it was in talks which could impact on its share price. The share price on Tuesday leapt 20 percent to 30 cents in busy trade of nearly 560,000 shares.
According to Bengoshi, there would be no substantial change in Sterling's business operations and the current management structure would stay in place.
The deal gained the support of South African Eagle Insurance Co Ltd, which holds a 20 percent stake in Sterling.
"It is no secret that the clothing industry is going through a rough time and the deal will help safeguard the position of Sterling personnel," said SA Eagles's Jim Carter.
The deal was seen giving Sterling added stability and direction, sponsoring broker Huysamer Stals said.
It added Bengoshi was expected to use Sterling as a vehicle to expand their operations in South Africa.

In the year to end-December Sterling's earnings slid to a 20 cents attributable loss per share from a 0.7 profit the year before. The firm said at the time that it had experienced its worst ever year due to industrial action and increasing volumes of illegal imports.
It did not forecast a to return to profitability in the first half of the new year, although it did expect the full year's bottom line to climb into the black.
